meta.name: ServiceNow Certified System Administrator (CSA)
meta.notes: [bulk-tag pass: added `servicenow-csa` tag to 61 questions] [recall sweep: 1 balanced rewrites]

questions.question: A company wants to use ServiceNow to automate IT service management across its enterprise. Which statement BEST describes what ServiceNow provides?
options: A customer relationship management (CRM) system for sales teams
A monitoring and alerting platform similar to Nagios or Zabbix
A cloud-based platform for IT Service Management and business process automation that digitizes workflows across the enterprise
A version control and software delivery pipeline tool
questions.explanation: ServiceNow is a cloud-based platform of record for enterprise service management. Originally focused on ITSM (IT Help Desk), it now spans HR, Customer Service, Legal, Security Operations, and custom applications. Its core value is digitizing workflows and replacing manual, email-based processes with automated, self-service, trackable service delivery.

questions.question: An administrator needs to test a new ServiceNow configuration before applying it to production users. What is the recommended approach for managing multiple ServiceNow environments?
options: Use the ServiceNow sandbox environment shared with all customers for testing
Purchase separate ServiceNow licenses for testing — each test requires a new instance
Maintain a 3-instance strategy: Development, Test/UAT, and Production,.
Use a single production instance with a test mode toggle in system properties
questions.explanation: ServiceNow recommends a 3-instance strategy: Development (customize and build), Test/UAT (quality assurance and user acceptance), and Production (live environment). Each instance is a separate, isolated deployment with its own database, URL (e.g., company.dev.service-now.com), and credentials. Changes are promoted from Dev→Test→Prod via Update Sets. each with its own database and URL

questions.question: A ServiceNow administrator needs to quickly navigate to the 'Incident' module in the classic UI. What is the FASTEST method?
options: Type 'incident' in the browser's URL bar after the instance domain
Use the left-side Application Navigator's filter bar to search for and find the Incident module
Navigate to System Definition > Tables and search for the incident table
Click the ServiceNow logo to access a full-text search of all modules
questions.explanation: The Application Navigator (left panel) has a filter/search bar at the top where you can type any application or module name and it instantly narrows the navigation tree. Typing 'Incident' immediately shows all incident-related modules. This is the fastest navigation method in the classic UI and is more direct than URL manipulation.

questions.question: A developer queries the ServiceNow incident table and needs to reference the assigned technician's email address in a script. The 'Assigned to' field on Incident is a Reference field pointing to sys_user. Which syntax accesses the email?
options: current.assigned_to_email
current.assigned_to.email using dot-walking through the reference field
sys_user.getEmail(current.assigned_to)
current.assigned_to + '@email'
questions.explanation: ServiceNow Reference fields store the sys_id of a related record. Dot-walking allows you to navigate across table relationships in scripts and reports. 'current.assigned_to.email' traverses from the Incident's assigned_to reference field into the sys_user table to retrieve the email value. This works in Business Rules, Client Scripts, and reports.

questions.question: A ServiceNow administrator needs to promote custom configurations (Business Rules, UI Policies, form layouts) from the Development instance to Production. What is the correct mechanism?
options: Export the database and import it into the Production instance
Use the ServiceNow Store to publish configurations from Development to Production
Package configuration changes in an Update Set.
Re-create all configurations manually in the Production instance
questions.explanation: Update Sets are containers that capture configuration changes (Business Rules, UI Policies, Client Scripts, workflows, form layouts, etc.) made while the Update Set is active. You export the Update Set as an XML file from Development, import it into Production, preview it for conflicts, then commit it. Note: Update Sets do NOT capture data records (incidents, users) — only configuration metadata. export it from Development, and import/commit it in Production

questions.question: A ServiceNow administrator needs to give the help desk team permission to read and create Incident records, but not access Change or Problem records. Which approach provides the MOST granular role-based control?
options: Create an ACL rule that denies all access to the Change table for help desk users
Assign the admin role to all help desk members for full access
Create a custom role with permissions only on the Incident table and assign it to the help desk group
Assign the 'itil' role for general ITSM access — it grants Incident, Change, and Problem access by default
questions.explanation: For granular role-based access, create a custom role with ACL rules that grant read/write/create access specifically on the Incident table. Assign this role to the help desk group — all group members inherit it. The 'itil' role grants broader access including Change and Problem, which violates the requirement. Custom roles allow you to define exactly which tables and operations are permitted.

questions.question: A ServiceNow Business Rule needs to automatically set the Incident Priority field to '1 - Critical' when Urgency is '1' and Impact is '1'. When should this Business Rule be configured to run?
options: Display Business Rule: runs when the form is displayed to pre-populate the priority
Client Script onChange: runs in the browser when urgency or impact fields change
Before Business Rule on insert/update: modifies the record in memory before it is saved to the database
Async Business Rule: runs in the background after the record saves
questions.explanation: A 'before' Business Rule runs server-side before the record is committed to the database. This is the correct timing for modifying field values that must be persisted — the script sets current.priority = '1' and it saves with the correct value. 'After' rules run post-save (can't modify the same record easily), 'async' runs in background, and Client Scripts run in the browser but can be bypassed.

questions.question: A service portal form has a 'Category' field that should make the 'Subcategory' field mandatory when 'Hardware' is selected. No JavaScript experience is required for the solution. Which feature should an administrator configure?
options: A Workflow with a condition checking the category value and pausing for subcategory input
A Client Script with an onChange handler that calls g_form.setMandatory('subcategory', true)
A UI Policy with condition 'Category is Hardware' and action 'Set Subcategory as Mandatory'
A Business Rule that sets a mandatory flag when category is 'Hardware'
questions.explanation: UI Policies are declarative (no-code) rules for controlling form behavior. You define a condition (Category = 'Hardware') and set actions (make Subcategory mandatory, read-only, or visible). UI Policies run client-side and require no JavaScript. They're the preferred tool for simple field behavior rules — Client Scripts should only be used when the logic exceeds UI Policy capabilities.

questions.question: An organization uses both legacy Workflows and the modern Flow Designer for process automation. When building a new approval process for service requests, which tool should the administrator use?
options: Workflow for ITSM processes, Flow Designer only for IT Operations processes
Both tools produce identical output and the choice is purely cosmetic
Flow Designer: modern low-code tool with triggers.
Legacy Workflow: more mature, supports all ITSM processes, and recommended for new development
questions.explanation: ServiceNow recommends Flow Designer for all new automation development. It uses a low-code, trigger-based model (record created/updated, scheduled, inbound email) with pre-built action steps (approvals, notifications, subflows, REST calls). While legacy Workflow is still supported for existing processes, new processes should be built in Flow Designer. Flow Designer also integrates with IntegrationHub spokes. actions, and subflows — recommended by ServiceNow for all new development

questions.question: A help desk manager wants to ensure the team responds to P1 incidents within 1 hour and resolves them within 4 hours. These timers should pause when incidents are put 'On Hold'. Which ServiceNow feature implements this?
options: A Scheduled Job that checks incident ages and sends notifications at thresholds
A Workflow with timer activities that count down from the incident creation time
A Business Rule that calculates elapsed time and triggers notifications via SNS
SLA Definitions configured with response and resolution durations.
questions.explanation: ServiceNow SLA Definitions specify: conditions for when the SLA applies, the schedule (business hours), start/pause/stop conditions (pause when state is 'On Hold', stop when state is 'Resolved'), and duration targets. The Task SLA table attaches to each qualifying incident and displays the percentage complete. Breach notifications are sent at configured thresholds (e.g., 75%, 100%). business schedules, and conditions that start, pause, and stop the timers based on incident state changes

questions.question: An administrator needs to send an automated email to the incident caller when their ticket is resolved. The email body should include the incident number, resolution notes, and caller's name. Which ServiceNow feature handles this?
options: An Outbound REST Message calling an external email service API
A Business Rule that calls gs.sendEmail() with a hardcoded message body
A Notification with a trigger condition (state = Resolved) and a message template using ${field_name} placeholders for incident data
A Scheduled Job that queries resolved incidents and sends emails via the SMTP relay
questions.explanation: ServiceNow Notifications are configured with: a table and trigger (Incident, when record is updated and State = Resolved), recipients (the Caller field), and a message template using ${number}, ${resolution_notes}, ${caller_id.name} placeholders. The system dynamically resolves these field references at send time. Notifications support HTML and are the standard, maintainable way to send automated emails.

questions.question: A SysAdmin is configuring ServiceNow Discovery to automatically find and populate servers and network devices in the CMDB. Which prerequisite must be in place before Discovery can scan the internal network?
options: A dedicated ServiceNow data center node co-located in the corporate data center
A ServiceNow agent installed on every device to be discovered
A MID Server installed on a VM inside the corporate network.
AWS Direct Connect between the ServiceNow cloud instance and the corporate network
questions.explanation: ServiceNow Discovery requires a MID Server — a Java application installed on a Windows or Linux VM inside the corporate network. The MID Server makes outbound HTTPS connections to the ServiceNow instance (no inbound ports needed) and uses protocols like SSH, WMI, SNMP, and JDBC to probe devices in the network ranges you configure. It acts as the bridge between the cloud instance and internal infrastructure. with outbound HTTPS access to the ServiceNow instance

questions.question: An administrator needs to restrict which incidents appear in a specific list view to only show incidents assigned to the current user. Where should this filter be configured for a persistent, role-based restriction?
options: In the user's personal preferences under List Filter settings
As an Access Control List (ACL) on the incident table with a condition script checking assigned_to == gs.getUserID()
As a personal list filter saved from the filter breadcrumbs in the list view
As a Database View that joins the incident table with the current user's assignments
questions.explanation: ACLs can include script conditions that evaluate at query time. An ACL on incident table 'read' operation with the condition script 'answer = (current.assigned_to == gs.getUserID())' ensures users only see incidents assigned to them — this applies globally to all list views, reports, and API queries for users with that restriction. Personal filters only affect the individual user's current session view.

questions.question: A ServiceNow Scheduled Job needs to run a GlideRecord query to close all incidents that have been in 'Resolved' state for more than 30 days. What is the CORRECT GlideRecord pattern for this query?
options: var gr = new GlideRecord('incident'); gr.get('state', '6'); gr.deleteRecord();
var gr = new GlideRecord('incident'); gr.addQuery('state'.
SELECT * FROM incident WHERE state = 5 AND resolved_at < DATEADD(day, -30, GETDATE())
GlideRecord.queryAll('incident').filter(state==5).close()
questions.explanation: GlideRecord is the server-side JavaScript API for querying and modifying ServiceNow database records. The pattern is: new GlideRecord(table), addQuery() for conditions, query() to execute, then while(gr.next()) to iterate results. gs.daysAgoStart(30) returns a GlideDateTime 30 days in the past for date comparisons. State value '5' = Resolved, '7' = Closed in default ServiceNow. '5'); gr.addQuery('resolved_at', '<', gs.daysAgoStart(30)); gr.query(); while(gr.next()) { gr.state = '7'; gr.update(); }

questions.question: A ServiceNow administrator needs to import user data from an HR system CSV file and create user records in sys_user. The CSV has columns named 'emp_id', 'full_name', and 'work_email'. What is the correct import process?
options: Directly upload the CSV to the sys_user table using the Import button on the Users list
Load the CSV into an Import Set.
Write a Business Rule that runs on insert to sys_user and populates fields from attached CSV data
Use the REST API to POST each CSV row individually to the User table endpoint
questions.explanation: ServiceNow's data import flow: (1) Load CSV into an Import Set staging table (raw data as strings), (2) Create a Transform Map that maps source columns to target table fields (emp_id→employee_number, full_name→name, work_email→email), (3) Run the transform to create/update records in sys_user. Coalesce fields prevent duplicate creation. This allows data review before committing to live tables. then create a Transform Map that maps emp_id→employee_number, full_name→name, work_email→email, and run the transform

questions.question: An employee reports that a button on the Incident form is not visible to them, but it appears for other technicians. The administrator checks and confirms the button is a UI Action. What is the MOST likely reason the button is hidden for this specific user?
options: The UI Action has a 'Condition' field with a role check that the user does not satisfy (e.g.
The user's browser does not support the button's JavaScript framework
The user's screen resolution is hiding the button at the bottom of the form
The button is controlled by a Workflow that is not currently active for this incident
questions.explanation: UI Actions (form buttons, related links, context menu items) support a 'Condition' field that determines when the action is displayed. A common pattern is gs.hasRole('itil') or specific role checks. If the user lacks the required role, the UI Action's condition evaluates to false and the button is not rendered. The administrator should check the UI Action's condition field against the user's assigned roles. condition: gs.hasRole('itil'))

questions.question: A company wants to track 'Mean Time to Resolve' (MTTR) for incidents over the past 12 months and visualize the trend with monthly data points. Which ServiceNow capability provides this time-based trending analysis?
options: A standard ServiceNow Report using a bar chart grouped by month
CloudWatch metrics integrated into ServiceNow via the Operations Management plugin
A GlideRecord script that calculates monthly averages and exports to a spreadsheet
Performance Analytics with an indicator defined on the MTTR metric.
questions.explanation: Performance Analytics is designed specifically for trending KPIs over time. You define an 'indicator' (e.g., average resolved_at - opened_at for incidents), configure a 'collector job' to snapshot the value on a schedule (monthly), and visualize historical trend data on dashboard widgets. Standard reports show point-in-time data only — they cannot show trends over historical periods without PA snapshots. using a data collector to snapshot values monthly

questions.question: A ServiceNow administrator configures a Transform Map for importing external data. The source system uses user ID '12345' but ServiceNow uses employee numbers formatted as 'EMP-12345'. How should the administrator handle this field transformation?
options: Modify the source CSV file to reformat IDs before importing
Use a Transform Map Field Map with an 'onBefore' script that prepends 'EMP-' to the source value before it is written to the target field
Create a GlideRecord lookup in a pre-transform script to find the matching user by both formats
Change the sys_user employee_number field format to accept plain numeric IDs
questions.explanation: Transform Map field maps support per-field transformation scripts. The 'onBefore' script runs before the field value is written to the target, giving you access to 'source.field_name' and allowing you to modify 'target.employee_number'. Setting target.employee_number = 'EMP-' + source.user_id applies the format transformation during import without modifying source data or target schema.

questions.question: A company wants employees to request access to enterprise applications through a self-service portal. Requests should route for manager approval and auto-provision access upon approval. Which ServiceNow module is purpose-built for this use case?
options: Change Management with a standard change template for access provisioning
Service Catalog with catalog items for each application.
CMDB with a CI relationship between users and applications they can access
Incident Management with a custom 'Access Request' category
questions.explanation: ServiceNow Service Catalog is purpose-built for self-service request management. Catalog items define what can be requested, variables capture required information (which app, justification, duration), Flow Designer handles the approval workflow (manager approval) and fulfillment actions (provisioning). Service requests generate RITM (Requested Item) records with full SLA tracking. variables for request details, and Flow Designer for approval and provisioning

questions.question: A user calls the help desk reporting they cannot access their email. The help desk agent creates a ticket. Which ServiceNow record type is MOST appropriate for this situation?
options: Change Request: modifies the email system configuration to restore access
Incident: responds to an unexpected interruption of the email service to restore normal service ASAP
Service Request (RITM): fulfills a user need for a standard service
Problem: investigates the root cause of an email system failure
questions.explanation: An Incident represents an unplanned interruption or degradation of an IT service. The goal is to restore service as quickly as possible (reactive). A Service Request is for requesting something new (proactive, expected). A Problem investigates recurring root causes. A Change is a planned modification. A user unable to access email = unplanned interruption = Incident.

questions.question: A ServiceNow Client Script needs to retrieve data from the server (e.g., look up a user's manager email when a name field changes) without causing a full form reload. Which API should be used?
options: GlideRecord directly in the Client Script (g_form.getReference works client-side)
A REST API call from the Client Script to the ServiceNow Table API endpoint
A Business Rule set to 'Display' timing that passes data through scratchpad
An AJAX call to a GlideAjax script include that runs server-side and returns data to the client
questions.explanation: Client Scripts run in the browser and cannot directly access the database. GlideAjax allows Client Scripts to make asynchronous calls to Script Includes on the server, which can perform GlideRecord queries and return data. The pattern is: create a Script Include extending AbstractAjaxProcessor, call it from the Client Script using GlideAjax with a callback function to handle the returned data without page reload.

questions.question: An IT Operations team wants to automatically restart a Windows service on a server whenever a related Incident is created and assigned to the 'Infrastructure' group. Which ServiceNow feature provides this server-side automation?
options: A Client Script that executes a remote command when the assignment group field changes
ServiceNow Orchestration with a PowerShell activity triggered from a Flow Designer flow or Workflow
A Scheduled Job that monitors incidents and restarts services every 5 minutes
A Business Rule that calls a REST API on the server to restart the service
questions.explanation: ServiceNow Orchestration runs automation activities on remote systems via the MID Server. A PowerShell activity can execute commands on Windows servers. This is triggered from Flow Designer (recommended) or a Workflow when an Incident is created and assigned to 'Infrastructure'. Orchestration handles authentication, execution, and result capture — no custom server-side REST endpoint is required.

questions.question: A large organization hosts multiple business units on a single ServiceNow instance. Each business unit should only see their own incidents, users, and configuration items — they must be completely isolated from each other. Which ServiceNow feature provides this multi-tenant isolation?
options: Using separate ServiceNow instances (one per business unit) with cross-instance integration
Creating separate application scopes for each business unit
Domain Separation, which partitions data so each domain can only see its own records while administrators can switch domain context
Assigning business-unit-specific roles that filter ACLs per unit
questions.explanation: Domain Separation is an enterprise feature that segregates data, processes, and administration between organizational units (domains) within a single ServiceNow instance. Users assigned to a domain only see records in their domain. Administrators can switch domain context to manage specific domains. This is commonly used by Managed Service Providers hosting multiple customers on one instance.

questions.question: A developer wants to add a 'Mark Duplicate' button to the Incident form that sets the state to 'Closed' and copies the duplicate incident number to the work notes. Which ServiceNow artifact should be created?
options: A UI Policy with actions that update the State and Work Notes fields
A UI Action (Form button) that runs a server-side script when clicked to update the record
A Business Rule that triggers when any Incident state changes to automatically handle duplicates
A Client Script of type 'onSubmit' that runs when the form is submitted
questions.explanation: UI Actions are buttons, related links, or context menu items that trigger scripts. A form button UI Action displays on the Incident form and, when clicked, runs a server-side script that can access and modify the current record (current.state = '7'; current.work_notes = '...'; current.update()). UI Actions can be configured to only show under certain conditions (e.g., only when state is 'In Progress').

questions.question: A ServiceNow Report needs to show the top 10 incident categories by volume for the current quarter. A manager also wants to see this report on their homepage dashboard with live data. How should this be set up?
options: Create a bar chart Report with a quarter filter.
Create the report, export it as PDF daily, and email it to the manager's homepage
Build a custom AngularJS widget in the Service Portal that queries the incident table
Create a Performance Analytics indicator that snapshots category counts daily
questions.explanation: ServiceNow Reports can be added as widgets to Homepages and Dashboards (Analytics Center). Create the report (bar chart, grouped by Category, filtered to current quarter), then on the Homepage, add a 'Report' gadget that references this saved report. The report runs with live data each time the homepage loads. This is the standard, no-code approach for management dashboards. then add it as a Report widget on the manager's ServiceNow Homepage or Analytics Center dashboard

questions.question: An administrator wants to import a large batch of configuration items (servers) from a CSV file into the CMDB. The import must avoid creating duplicate CI records if a CI with the same hostname already exists. What field mapping option prevents duplicates?
options: Enable the 'Coalesce' flag on the hostname field in the Transform Map.
Add a 'Check for duplicates' condition in the Transform Script
Set the Transform Map's 'Run business rules' option to Yes so Business Rules handle deduplication
Create a Before Transform script that deletes all existing CI records before importing
questions.explanation: The 'Coalesce' option on a Transform Map field map designates that field as a match key. When transforming an import row, if a record in the target table already has the same coalesced field value (hostname), the transform UPDATES that existing record instead of creating a new one. This prevents duplicate CI creation. Multiple fields can be coalesced together for compound match keys. which uses it as a match key to update existing CIs instead of creating new ones

questions.question: The IT Director needs a ServiceNow homepage that shows a real-time count of open P1 incidents, a gauge showing SLA breach percentage, and a list of today's unassigned incidents. Which homepage components should be used?
options: Add Report gadgets and Gauge gadgets to a shared Dashboard.
Create separate full-page reports for each metric and bookmark them in the browser
Use Performance Analytics indicators for real-time counts (note: PA requires scheduled snapshots, not real-time)
Embed SQL queries in the ServiceNow homepage using the Script Console gadget
questions.explanation: ServiceNow Homepages (and the Analytics Center) support widgets including Report gadgets (show any saved report), Gauge gadgets (semi-circle with target values), and Activity Stream gadgets. Each gadget points to a saved report with appropriate filters. The Director can have this shared dashboard deployed to their homepage. Gadgets refresh each time the page loads, showing live data. each widget points to a saved report with the appropriate filter conditions

questions.question: An employee wants to submit a new laptop request through a modern, consumer-style web interface. The IT administrator has configured the laptop as a catalog item. Which ServiceNow interface is designed for this end-user self-service experience?
options: Service Portal, a modern responsive web interface with a widget-based layout designed for end-user self-service
The ServiceNow mobile app exclusive to iOS only
ServiceNow Agent workspace designed for ITSM professionals
The classic ServiceNow UI (UI16) where employees access the Employee Center module
questions.explanation: Service Portal is ServiceNow's modern, responsive web interface built with AngularJS widgets. It's designed for end-users (not IT staff) with a clean consumer-style UI, mobile-friendly layout, and a self-service focus (catalog browsing, ticket submission, knowledge articles). Organizations customize portals with branded widgets. The classic UI (UI16/Polaris) is the administration and IT operations interface.

questions.question: A development team is building a custom application on ServiceNow. The platform architect recommends building it in a 'scoped application' rather than the global scope. What is the PRIMARY reason for this recommendation?
options: The global scope has been deprecated and will be removed in a future release
Scoped applications can only be accessed by administrators, providing better security
Scoped applications run faster due to isolated memory allocation
Scoped applications isolate customizations in their own namespace.
questions.explanation: Scoped applications have their own namespace prefix (e.g., x_acme_appname). Scripts and tables within the scope are isolated from other applications, preventing naming conflicts with platform upgrades or other customizations. Scoped apps can be distributed via the ServiceNow App Store. The global scope is still supported but is not recommended for new development because global customizations can conflict with each other and with platform upgrades. preventing naming conflicts and making the app portable and publishable to the ServiceNow Store

questions.question: A ServiceNow administrator is implementing an Incident Management process. According to ITIL principles supported by ServiceNow, what is the PRIMARY goal of Incident Management?
options: To restore normal service operation as quickly as possible and minimize business impact
To plan and implement changes to IT infrastructure with minimal disruption
To track the configuration and relationships of all IT infrastructure components
To identify and eliminate the root cause of recurring infrastructure failures
questions.explanation: ITIL Incident Management's primary goal is to restore normal service operation as quickly as possible and minimize the impact of the incident on business operations. It is reactive — the focus is resolution speed, not root cause analysis (that is Problem Management's goal). ServiceNow Incident workflows, SLAs, and escalation rules are all designed around this ITIL principle.

questions.question: A recurring incident reveals that a known web server configuration causes periodic crashes. The team resolves the incident each time but has not fixed the underlying issue. According to ITIL, what record type should be created to investigate and permanently fix the root cause?
options: A Change Request to immediately fix the configuration
A Service Request to the vendor for a permanent patch
A Problem record to track root cause investigation.
A duplicate Incident linking all recurring crashes together
questions.explanation: In ITIL, Problem Management is responsible for investigating the root cause of one or more incidents. A Problem record is created to investigate 'why is this recurring'. Once the root cause is identified, a Known Error record documents the cause and workaround. A Change Request is then raised to implement the permanent fix. This separation of Incident (restore service) vs Problem (fix root cause) is fundamental ITIL. with a Known Error record when the cause is identified

questions.question: A ServiceNow administrator needs to connect ServiceNow to Jira Cloud so that when an Incident is resolved in ServiceNow, a corresponding Jira issue is automatically created. Which ServiceNow product provides pre-built Jira integration actions?
options: Outbound REST Message configured manually with Jira's API endpoints and authentication
MID Server JDBC probe querying the Jira database directly
ServiceNow Scripted REST APIs that call the Jira REST API via custom JavaScript
IntegrationHub with the Jira spoke.
questions.explanation: IntegrationHub extends Flow Designer with pre-built 'spokes' for popular third-party systems. The Jira spoke includes actions like 'Create Issue', 'Update Issue', 'Get Issue', and 'Add Comment'. In Flow Designer, you trigger on Incident state change (Resolved), then use the Jira 'Create Issue' action. This requires minimal code and the Jira spoke handles OAuth, API versioning, and error handling. providing pre-built Flow Designer actions for creating, updating, and querying Jira issues

questions.question: A Service Catalog administrator creates a laptop request catalog item. Multiple other catalog items (phone requests, monitor requests) also need the same set of fields: Department, Business Justification, and Manager Approval. What is the MOST efficient way to reuse these fields?
options: Create a Variable Set containing the shared fields and include it in all relevant catalog items
Create a parent catalog item that other items inherit from using ServiceNow's OOP inheritance
Copy and re-create the same variables on each catalog item individually
Build a single 'Hardware Request' catalog item that serves all hardware request types
questions.explanation: Variable Sets are reusable groups of catalog item variables. You create the Variable Set once (Department, Business Justification, Manager Approval) and include it in any number of catalog items. Changes to the Variable Set are automatically reflected in all catalog items that include it. This follows the DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself) principle and makes maintenance much simpler than duplicating variables.

questions.question: A ServiceNow CMDB is being used for change impact analysis. Before approving a change to a database server, the change manager wants to know which applications depend on it. Which CMDB feature provides this dependency mapping?
options: The Discovery dashboard showing discovery history for the server
The CMDB Timeline view showing when the server CI was last modified
A GlideRecord query on the cmdb_ci table filtering by CI class
The CI Relationship map (Dependency View) showing upstream and downstream CIs connected to the database server
questions.explanation: The ServiceNow CMDB stores relationships between CIs (e.g., Application Server 'depends on' Database Server). The CI Dependency View (Relationship map) graphically displays these upstream and downstream relationships. Change managers use this to understand blast radius — what other CIs (applications, services, business services) could be impacted by a change to the database server CI.

questions.question: A ServiceNow Knowledge Base article is being written to document the workaround for a common printer connectivity issue. What is the correct WORKFLOW for publishing the article so end users can find it in the Service Portal?
options: Post the article in the Service Portal's announcement section directly
Create the article in Draft.
Write the article in Microsoft Word and upload it as an attachment to the Knowledge Base
Create the article and it immediately appears in the Service Portal upon save
questions.explanation: ServiceNow Knowledge Management uses a workflow: Draft (author creates content) → In Review (submitted for peer/manager review) → Published (live and searchable). The exact workflow varies by Knowledge Base configuration, but requiring review/approval before publication is the standard best practice. Only Published articles appear in Service Portal searches and are visible to end users. submit for review, have a knowledge manager approve it, then publish — making it searchable in the Service Portal

questions.question: An administrator is configuring Change Management for a company with a Change Advisory Board (CAB). Emergency changes that cannot wait for the weekly CAB meeting should be approved by just two on-call managers. How should this be configured in ServiceNow?
options: Create a single Change record type that the CAB reviews for all changes regardless of urgency
Use the standard Normal change approval flow with an emergency flag that reduces SLA timers
Configure an Emergency change type with a separate approval workflow that routes to an Emergency CAB (ECAB) or on-call approver group with a defined quorum of 2
Allow technicians to bypass approvals for emergency changes by granting them the change_admin role
questions.explanation: ServiceNow Change Management supports multiple change types: Normal (full CAB review), Standard (pre-approved, low-risk), and Emergency (expedited approval). Emergency changes have a separate workflow that routes to an Emergency CAB (ECAB) — typically a smaller group of approvers available 24/7. The approval rule can be configured with 'quorum' (2 out of N approvers required) to match the company's requirement.

questions.question: A MID Server is installed on a Windows VM inside the corporate network. The Discovery probe fails to connect to Linux servers via SSH. The credentials are stored in ServiceNow. What should the administrator verify FIRST?
options: That the Windows MID Server VM has network connectivity (TCP port 22) to the target Linux servers and that the SSH credentials stored in ServiceNow Discovery Credentials are correct
That the MID Server has an inbound firewall rule allowing traffic from ServiceNow's IP range
That the Linux servers have the SSM agent installed
That the ServiceNow instance has a valid SSL certificate for HTTPS communication
questions.explanation: The MID Server initiates SSH connections from its location (inside the corporate network) to target devices. The MID Server must have network access to the target hosts on port 22, and the SSH credentials stored in ServiceNow (Discovery > Credentials) must be valid for the target Linux servers. The MID Server only requires outbound HTTPS to ServiceNow — inbound from ServiceNow is not needed.

questions.question: A company's ServiceNow administrator notices that a Business Rule is running on every page load in the Service Portal, significantly degrading performance. What is the MOST appropriate Business Rule timing for checking a condition and notifying users without impacting page load performance?
options: Change the Business Rule to 'Before' timing to run before any database operation
Change the Business Rule to 'Async' timing.
Convert the Business Rule to a Client Script so it runs in the browser instead
Change the Business Rule to 'Display' timing — it runs only when forms are displayed and caches data in scratchpad
questions.explanation: Async Business Rules run in a background thread after the triggering database operation completes. They do not block the user's request/response cycle. For tasks like sending notifications, calling external APIs, or performing heavy calculations that don't need to modify the triggering record, async is the correct choice. Before/After rules run synchronously within the transaction, adding latency to the user's experience. it runs in a background thread after the record operation, not during the page load

questions.question: A ServiceNow administrator needs to give a vendor's application in another account read-only access to the ServiceNow REST API to sync incident data. The vendor should use OAuth 2.0 for authentication. What should the administrator configure?
options: Configure an OAuth 2.0 Application Registry (OAuth application) in ServiceNow.
Create an Integration User with basic auth credentials and share them with the vendor
Enable ServiceNow REST API public access in System Web Services settings
Create an API key in ServiceNow and add it to HTTP headers for all vendor requests
questions.explanation: ServiceNow supports OAuth 2.0 via the Application Registry (System OAuth > Application Registry). You create an OAuth application specifying the grant type (e.g., Client Credentials or Password), generate a client_id and client_secret, and configure token expiry. The vendor exchanges credentials for a bearer token and includes it in API requests. This is more secure than basic auth as tokens expire and can be revoked. generate client credentials, and provide the vendor with the client_id and client_secret for the OAuth flow

questions.question: After a major incident affecting 500+ users, the problem management team wants to conduct a post-incident review. In ServiceNow, which record type is used to document root cause analysis, remediation steps, and prevent future recurrence?
options: A Problem record for root cause investigation.
The original Incident record, updated with root cause and prevention notes
A Change Request documenting what went wrong and how it was fixed
A Service Request documenting the remediation tasks assigned to the infrastructure team
questions.explanation: ITIL Problem Management uses Problem records for root cause analysis (RCA). The workflow: (1) Problem record created for investigation, (2) Known Error record documents the verified cause and workaround, (3) Change Request raised for permanent fix. The Problem record links to all related incidents, tracks the RCA documentation, and measures time to resolution. This separates reactive incident resolution from proactive root cause analysis. with a linked Known Error record and eventual Change Request for permanent fix

questions.question: A company uses a custom table 'x_vendor_orders' in a scoped application. A Global scope Business Rule needs to read from this table. What must the scoped application developer configure to allow this cross-scope access?
options: Create a Scripted REST API in the scoped app that the global Business Rule can call via HTTP
Nothing — global scope has unrestricted access to all tables including scoped application tables
The developer must grant 'Cross-Scope Access' on the scoped table.
The global Business Rule must be moved to the scoped application's scope to access the table
questions.explanation: By default, scoped application tables are not accessible by other scopes (including global). The scoped app developer must explicitly configure Cross-Scope Access: navigate to the scoped table's application access settings, add the 'global' scope (or specific scopes) as allowed callers, and specify which operations (read, create, write, delete) are permitted. This maintains application isolation while allowing controlled access. specifying the 'global' scope as an allowed caller and the permitted operations (read)

questions.question: A ServiceNow administrator creates a list view for Incidents and wants to save the current filter (Assigned to = Current User AND State = In Progress) as a shortcut for the entire IT team. How should this be saved?
options: Save it as a public filter from the filter breadcrumbs.
Create a saved search in the Application Navigator for the team
Save it as a Personal filter — team members must recreate it individually on their own accounts
Save the URL with the query parameters and share it with the team via email
questions.explanation: ServiceNow list view filters can be saved from the filter breadcrumbs using 'Save as filter'. Saving as a 'public' filter makes it visible to all users in the filter selector dropdown. Saving as 'global' makes it the default view. Personal filters are only visible to the creating user. Public filters are the standard way to share commonly used list views across a team. making it available to all users with access to the Incident list

questions.question: A company uses ServiceNow Event Management. An external monitoring tool sends events via REST to ServiceNow when a server goes down. What does Event Management do with these incoming events?
options: Stores events in the 'em_event' table.
Directly creates Incident records from each incoming event
Forwards events to the MID Server for on-premises processing
Sends push notifications to technicians' mobile devices with the raw event data
questions.explanation: ServiceNow Event Management receives raw events into the 'em_event' table. Event rules and correlation rules analyze incoming events, deduplicate noise (many events for the same issue create one alert), and apply thresholds. Significant alerts can automatically create OpsItems (Operations Management) or trigger Incident creation. This prevents alert storms from flooding the help desk with thousands of tickets from a single infrastructure failure. correlates related events, applies alert rules, and can automatically create Incidents or OpsItems for significant correlated alerts

questions.question: A ServiceNow administrator needs to configure the system so that all users in the 'Network Team' group are automatically assigned as approvers for Change Requests affecting network devices. How should this approval requirement be implemented?
options: Manually assign the Network Team group to each Change Request when it is created
Grant the Network Team admin role so they can approve any Change
Configure an Approval Rule or Flow Designer flow that adds the 'Network Team' group as an approver when the Change record contains network device CIs or a specific category value
Create a Business Rule that adds a journal note to Changes affecting network devices
questions.explanation: Change approval workflows in ServiceNow (in legacy Workflow or Flow Designer) support dynamic approval rules. An approval rule or flow step can evaluate conditions (e.g., Category = 'Network' or affected CI class = Network Device) and dynamically add the 'Network Team' group as an approver. Group-based approvals require any or all members to approve based on the quorum setting.

questions.question: A company's ServiceNow system property 'glide.ui.activity.stream.enabled' needs to be changed in Production. A junior admin changes it directly in Production without using an Update Set. What problem does this create?
options: No problem — system properties are always environment-specific and do not need Update Sets
The change will be automatically reverted during the next ServiceNow upgrade
ServiceNow automatically creates an Update Set for all system property changes
System properties changed without an Update Set are not captured and cannot be easily replicated or rolled back through the normal Dev→Test→Prod promotion process
questions.explanation: System properties changed outside an active Update Set are not captured in any Update Set. This means: the change cannot be documented or rolled back via Update Sets, and if Production needs to be restored or a similar change needs to be made in Dev/Test, it must be done manually. Best practice is always to make configuration changes (including system properties) while an Update Set is active in the appropriate environment.

questions.question: A ServiceNow instance is being upgraded to a new platform version. The upgrade process detects conflicts between the new platform code and customizations made in the global scope. What is the recommended approach for handling these upgrade conflicts?
options: Contact ServiceNow support to have them manually merge the conflicts
Reject all platform updates to preserve customizations, creating a permanent fork from the platform
Accept all platform updates and delete all customizations — start fresh after each upgrade
Review each conflict in the 'Upgrade Monitor'.
questions.explanation: During upgrades, the Upgrade Monitor shows all conflicts between platform updates and global customizations. For each conflict, you can review the diff, accept the platform version (losing your customization), skip the platform update (keeping your customization), or accept and then reapply your logic. This is why ServiceNow recommends building customizations in scoped applications — scoped apps don't conflict with platform updates. evaluate the changes, and use the 'Skip' or 'Accept' options — then reapply essential customizations using scoped applications for future upgrades

questions.question: A manager needs to be notified by email when any Incident they are the 'Manager of caller' for is escalated to Priority 1. The notification should reference the incident number and short description. Which notification configuration achieves this?
options: Create a Notification with table = Incident.
Create a Scheduled Job that checks for P1 incidents every minute and emails managers
Configure an SLA breach notification for P1 incidents addressed to all managers
Create a Business Rule that calls gs.sendEmail() whenever priority changes to 1
questions.explanation: ServiceNow Notifications support multiple recipient types including 'Field value' which allows dot-walking through reference fields (caller_id.manager retrieves the caller's manager). The notification triggers when Priority = '1 - Critical', includes the manager via dot-walked field, and uses ${number}/${short_description} template placeholders. This is declarative with no custom scripting required. condition = Priority = 1-Critical, recipient = 'Manager of caller' (a recipient field type that navigates caller_id.manager), and message template with ${number} and ${short_description}

questions.question: An organization wants all employees to be able to view an IT status page in ServiceNow that shows ongoing incidents and planned maintenance. The page should be accessible without logging in. Which ServiceNow feature enables this public, unauthenticated access?
options: Configure a ServiceNow Service Portal page with 'Public' access role enabled.
Share a saved Incident report URL that bypasses authentication
Enable anonymous API access on the Table API for the incident table
Create a public Knowledge Base article that lists current incidents
questions.explanation: ServiceNow Service Portal pages can be configured with roles including 'public', which allows unauthenticated access. A status portal built on Service Portal with widgets displaying active incidents and maintenance windows can be made accessible without login credentials. The portal builder controls which pages are public vs. requiring authentication. This is the standard pattern for customer/employee-facing status pages. allowing unauthenticated browsing

questions.question: A ServiceNow admin needs to report on SLA compliance — specifically the percentage of P2 incidents resolved within the 4-hour SLA target, broken down by assignment group, over the last 90 days. Which ServiceNow table contains the SLA tracking data for this report?
options: The 'sys_metric_instance' table used by Performance Analytics
The 'incident' table with a calculated field for resolution time
The 'sla_definition' table which stores target durations
The 'task_sla' table, which stores SLA records attached to each task (incident) with breach status, elapsed time, and business elapsed time
questions.explanation: The 'task_sla' table stores individual SLA records for each task (Incident, Change, etc.) that matches an SLA Definition. Each task_sla record contains: the related incident, SLA definition, start/end times, business elapsed time, whether the SLA was breached, and the breach percentage. Reports built on the task_sla table with filters for Priority = P2 and Assignment Group provide accurate SLA compliance data.

questions.question: A company is going live with ServiceNow ITSM for the first time. The project team asks what data should NOT be transported via Update Sets when migrating configuration from Development to Production.
options: Data records such as user accounts.
Form layouts and list view configurations
Workflows and Flow Designer flows
Business Rules, Client Scripts, and UI Policies
questions.explanation: Update Sets capture metadata/configuration changes (Business Rules, Workflows, form layouts, etc.) but NOT data records. User accounts, groups, incidents, service catalog request records, and environment-specific system properties (URLs, passwords, credentials) should NOT be transported via Update Sets. Data migration requires separate tools (data import with Import Sets, manual configuration per environment, or Automated Test Framework). groups, existing incidents, catalog items' variable values, and system properties with environment-specific values

questions.question: A ServiceNow administrator needs to restrict a field on the Incident form so that only members of the 'Management' role can edit the 'Business Impact' field. All other roles can view but not modify it. Which feature enforces this field-level restriction?
options: A form section that is hidden from non-management users using ServiceNow Views
A Field-level Access Control List (ACL) on incident.business_impact with write permission requiring the 'management' role
A Business Rule that reverts changes to the field unless the user has the Management role
A UI Policy that makes the field read-only for all users except Management
questions.explanation: Field-level ACLs control read and write access to specific fields on a table. An ACL on 'incident.business_impact' with operation 'write' and a role requirement of 'management' prevents users without that role from editing the field. Since the ACL is for write only, users without the role can still read (view) the field. This is the correct, server-enforced (not just UI-enforced) security control.

questions.question: A ServiceNow instance has slow response times. A developer suspects a Business Rule with an unoptimized GlideRecord query is running on every Incident form view. How should the developer identify the problematic Business Rule?
options: Enable JavaScript Debugger in the browser developer tools to trace execution
Review the CMDB for dependencies that might be causing the slowdown
Check the ServiceNow System Log for error messages related to the slow form
Use the ServiceNow Performance Diagnostics (Stats.do or Transaction Log in System Logs > Transactions) to identify slow transactions and the contributing scripts
questions.explanation: ServiceNow's Transaction Log (System Logs > Transactions) shows execution time for all transactions including which Business Rules, Client Scripts, and ACLs ran and their individual durations. The 'stats.do' page provides runtime statistics. This allows developers to identify exactly which Business Rule is consuming the most time per transaction. System Log errors would show JavaScript exceptions, not performance issues.

questions.question: A company wants to use ServiceNow to manage software license compliance. The CMDB should track which software is installed on which servers and alert when license counts are exceeded. Which ServiceNow product addresses this?
options: ServiceNow Strategic Portfolio Management for software spend tracking
ServiceNow Security Operations for vulnerability management of unlicensed software
ServiceNow Software Asset Management (SAM).
ServiceNow IT Operations Management (ITOM) Event Management
questions.explanation: ServiceNow Software Asset Management (SAM) is designed for software license compliance. It uses Discovery data (software installs from the CMDB) and compares against purchased license entitlements. SAM generates compliance positions (over-licensed or under-licensed), tracks software spend, and identifies reclamation opportunities. It integrates with the CMDB and supports software normalization to handle variations in product names. which tracks software installs discovered via Discovery and compares them against license entitlements

questions.question: A ServiceNow Flow Designer flow needs to call a third-party REST API and handle a potential 429 (Too Many Requests) response by retrying after 30 seconds. Which flow capability handles this?
options: Use a subflow with error handling that catches the 429 status and schedules a delayed re-execution
Configure the REST step's retry settings with exponential backoff — Flow Designer REST steps have built-in retry configuration
Add a Condition step after the REST call that checks the response code and uses a Wait step + Loop to retry
Handle retry logic in an IntegrationHub spoke action's built-in error handling configuration
questions.explanation: In Flow Designer, after a REST API call step, you can add a Decision/If condition that evaluates the response code. If the code is 429, a Wait step pauses execution for 30 seconds, then a Go-to or Loop step retries the API call. Flow Designer doesn't natively have configurable retry with wait periods built into REST steps — this logic is assembled from Flow Designer primitives (condition + wait + loop).

questions.question: An administrator clones the Production ServiceNow instance to the Development instance to refresh Development with current data. After cloning, what must the administrator do BEFORE the Development team continues working?
options: Restore a backup of the Development database from before the clone to preserve in-progress work
Run the post-clone cleanup tasks: update instance-specific system properties (URLs.
Re-enable all active Update Sets that were preserved from the pre-clone Development configuration
Nothing — the cloned instance is ready to use immediately after the clone completes
questions.explanation: After cloning, the Development instance has Production's data and configuration, including Production-specific settings. Post-clone tasks are critical: update system properties (instance URL, SMTP relay, integration OAuth endpoints) to Development values, re-enable excluded customizations, reset integration credentials that should differ from Production, and exclude/disable any scheduled jobs that should not run in Development (e.g., production integrations). integration credentials, SMTP settings), reactivate excluded Update Sets, and verify all integrations point to non-production endpoints

questions.question: A ServiceNow virtual agent chatbot is being deployed to help employees self-resolve common IT issues. Which ServiceNow product provides this conversational AI interface and integrates natively with the Service Catalog and Knowledge Base?
options: ServiceNow Virtual Agent with NLU (Natural Language Understanding) model and pre-built topic conversations that can search Knowledge articles, create tickets, and submit catalog requests
ServiceNow IntegrationHub with a chatbot spoke connecting to an external NLP service
ServiceNow Service Portal with a custom AngularJS chat widget
ServiceNow Automated Test Framework for simulating user interactions
questions.explanation: ServiceNow Virtual Agent is a native chatbot platform built on NLU (Natural Language Understanding). It includes pre-built topic conversations for common ITSM tasks (reset password, report outage, request access). Virtual Agent integrates with Knowledge Base (searches articles based on user query), Service Catalog (submit requests), and Incident Management (create/status check tickets) natively within ServiceNow.

questions.question: A ServiceNow project is about to go live. The UAT team discovers that 3 of the 50 Update Set changes conflict with an existing customization in the Test instance. What is the recommended approach?
options: Commit all Update Sets ignoring conflicts and fix issues in Production after go-live
Delete all conflicting Update Sets and rebuild the affected configurations from scratch in Production
Merge all Update Sets into a single batch Update Set to avoid individual conflicts
Preview each Update Set in the Test instance.
questions.explanation: The correct Update Set deployment process is: (1) Load/upload the Update Set XML into the target instance, (2) Preview the Update Set — ServiceNow identifies potential conflicts and shows a preview log, (3) Resolve conflicts (decide which version of conflicting records to use), (4) Commit. This preview step is critical — never skip it in Production. Update Sets with unresolved conflicts can overwrite important configurations. review the conflicts in the Preview log, resolve them (choose which version to keep), then commit in the correct order

questions.question: A company uses ServiceNow's Configuration Management Database (CMDB) as its System of Record for IT infrastructure. After a server is decommissioned, what should happen to its CI record in the CMDB?
options: Set the CI's Operational Status to 'Retired' or 'Decommissioned'.
Delete the CI record permanently from the CMDB to keep the database clean
Move the CI record to a 'Retired' class in the CMDB by changing the operational status
Archive the CI by exporting it to an Excel file and then deleting it from ServiceNow
questions.explanation: CIs should never be deleted from the CMDB — they represent infrastructure history. When a server is decommissioned, set its Operational Status to 'Retired' or the CI lifecycle status to 'Retired'. This preserves: the CI's configuration history, incident/change/problem history (via CI relationships), audit trail, and CMDB reporting accuracy. Reports can filter out Retired CIs for current infrastructure views. this preserves the CI's history and relationships while marking it inactive

questions.question: A ServiceNow script needs to log a debug message that appears in the System Log when a specific condition is met. Which function is the CORRECT way to write to the ServiceNow System Log from a server-side script?
options: console.log('Debug message') — the same as browser JavaScript logging
ServiceNow.writeLog('Debug message') using the platform's logging API
gs.log('Debug message', 'source_name') or gs.debug('Debug message') to write to the ServiceNow System Log with appropriate log level
new GlideRecord('sys_log').insert() to directly insert a log record
questions.explanation: The GlideSystem (gs) API provides server-side logging methods: gs.log() (informational), gs.debug() (debug level — only visible if debug logging is enabled), gs.warn() (warning), and gs.error() (error). These write to System Logs > System Log and are the standard way to add logging to Business Rules, Script Includes, and Scheduled Jobs. console.log() does not work in server-side ServiceNow scripts.

questions.question: A new employee starts at a company. Their onboarding requires: creating a user account in Active Directory, provisioning a laptop from the hardware catalog, granting access to 3 business applications, and scheduling a welcome meeting. All these tasks should be managed from a single ServiceNow process. Which ServiceNow product best orchestrates this multi-department, multi-step onboarding workflow?
options: Change Management with a Normal change template for all new employee onboardings
A single Service Catalog item with 4 variables asking for all required information
ITSM Incident Management with one incident per onboarding task
ServiceNow HR Service Delivery (HRSD) with a case and multi-step playbook coordinating tasks across IT,.
questions.explanation: ServiceNow HR Service Delivery (HRSD) is designed for lifecycle events like onboarding. It uses 'Case Management' with 'Playbooks' — structured, multi-step workflows that coordinate tasks across departments (IT, Facilities, HR). Each task is assigned to the appropriate team, tracked to completion, and the overall onboarding case provides a single view of all activities. HRSD integrates with the Service Catalog for provisioning requests and with Orchestration for automated provisioning. Facilities, and HR departments from a single record

questions.question: In ServiceNow's out-of-the-box ITIL implementation, certain default roles can RESOLVE incidents (change incident state to Resolved) while others only view them. Which TWO out-of-the-box roles can resolve incidents?
options: `itil` — the baseline ITIL fulfiller role; can update and resolve incidents
`itil_admin` — an administrative ITIL role; can update and resolve incidents (and configure ITIL processes)
`itil_viewer` (or equivalent read-only role) — read-only access; CANNOT resolve incidents
`employee` / `ess` — end-user self-service; can submit but not resolve incidents
questions.explanation: The `itil` role is the standard fulfiller role that can update and resolve incidents. `itil_admin` inherits it and adds admin capabilities. `itil_self_service` (sometimes called `itil_user`) is for end-users opening tickets — they cannot resolve. `itil_external` is for read-only external collaborators.
